v.why: Removing an edge that already carries nothing costs nothing, unlike removing a live edge.
Deleting an edge feeding a dead-end node costs nothing.
With 1->3 absent, edge 0 has fewer routes to the output, so strengthening it matters more.
Cutting edge 0 removes node 1's only remaining route to the output when edge 4 is already gone, so the loss is larger.
Another conv into the output node has diminishing returns when a conv from node 2 is already there.
A skip is already a strong op on this edge, so replacing it with a conv gains less than replacing none or pooling.
With a direct skip 0->3 as a fallback, removing edge 5 costs less.
A strong direct conv 0->3 covers for the removed edge, so the loss is smaller.
Edges 4 and 5 are parallel feeders of node 3 and substitute for each other.
Deleting a strong conv on the direct edge hurts more than deleting a weak op.
